text:
oncall-bot: incident-bot: page fired for service="gpu-inference-dedicated" alert="GPU memory pressure > 90%" pool="ded-az1" alert_id=PD12345

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Triggered alert PD12345 (gpu-inference-dedicated) — paging primary on-call

sam wang: acked — I’m on it, looking at ded-az1 dashboard now.

jess ramos: I see a very short spike in KV cache fills around 17:32 UTC, could be a single noisy job. No obvious widespread latency increase yet.

leo nguyen: infra metrics: GPU mem usage jumped to 92% for ~18s, then auto-resolved. But PD fired on the single sample rule (1m).

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Alert PD12345 auto-resolved (duration ~45s)

oncall-bot: incident-bot: alert PD12346 fired for same rule on pool=ded-az1 (possible flapping)

sam wang: seeing the second firing — this looks like flapping. I'm going to mute immediate repeats and check in-flight batches.

jess ramos: can we temporarily reduce batch_concurrency for ded-az1 to shed some memory pressure? If it's a noisy eval job, that should help.

sam wang: reducing batch_concurrency from 6 -> 2 for pool=ded-az1

```
# command run on control plane
redwoodctl pools update ded-az1 --batch-concurrency 2
```

leo nguyen: changed autoscaler policy to allow +1 warm node on pressure spikes (min_capacity unchanged). That should give extra headroom for short bursts.

maria d'souza: confirmed: memory usage dropped back to ~55% after the concurrency tweak and autoscaler kick. No customer-facing 5xx spikes in the last 3m. Marking impact: low.

sam wang: thanks. I'm going to add a short debounce on the alert rule (require 3/2m) so PD doesn't spam for transient 1-sample spikes.

oncall-bot: incident-bot: alert PD12346 auto-resolved

jess ramos: agree on debounce. Also adding an anomaly filter to ignore short-lived KV cache flush patterns we saw in the logs.

leo nguyen: logs show one internal eval harness from team-x kicked off at 17:31:27 that hit a pathological prompt length; notified team-x in #eng about optimizing.

sam wang: handoff note for next on-call: monitor ded-az1 for 2 more hours, if flapping repeats escalate to eng-sre and open a quick RCA ticket. Maria, can you take handoff? @maria d'souza

maria d'souza: taking handoff. I'll keep an eye and follow up in the morning if anything persists. Adding a follow-up todo: tune alert rule + add runbook snippet for temporary concurrency change.

sam wang: thanks all. Summary: transient GPU memory spike from noisy eval job caused two quick PD pages, auto-resolved after reducing batch_concurrency and autoscaler added a node. Impact: low, no sustained customer errors. Mitigations: debounce alert rule, anomaly filter, notify team-x to optimize job. Closing thread unless it reappears. :white_check_mark:
